title: 4. Article 13 – Laws Inconsistent with Fundamental Rights

blocks.content:
Article 13 declares that any law violating Fundamental Rights is void.
This establishes the doctrine of judicial review.
Article 13 declares that any law violating Fundamental Rights is void.

items: Article 13 is frequently tested as the constitutional basis for the doctrine of judicial review.
Questions often focus on the legal consequence (being declared void) of laws that violate Fundamental Rights under Article 13.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 13 mandates that any law inconsistent with Fundamental Rights is rendered void.
This constitutional provision serves as the foundation for the doctrine of judicial review.
